prize_parts.citation: for the conception of targeted protein degradation, in which heterobifunctional small molecules direct ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins
for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I keep the two-part configuration from round 1, and the round-1 exchange has made me more certain about the shape of each part. Targeted protein degradation has the broadest support in the committee, and I share the view that the support rests on substance: a small molecule induces a ligase-target ternary complex and event-driven catalysis replaces occupancy-based inhibition. The concept that defines that principle is the 2001 PROTAC proposal of Crews and Deshaies, so I anchor the part there and cite bifunctional degraders. Base editing is a separate chemical principle, hydrolytic deamination of a base on a single-stranded R-loop, engineered by directed evolution of a deaminase to act on DNA. It is independently replicated, in routine use, and already in patients. The decisive conceptual and experimental program is Liu's, so a single name is the cleanest attribution. The three people are the maximum, and none of them is a compromise placeholder.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to my configuration is the one the chair raised: five members want B020 alone, and a combined prize can look like splitting the field for balance. I do not think that is a sufficient reason to merge, but I accept that the pairing of two therapeutic-adjacent fields carries presentist risk. For B020, leaving out Handa, Ito and Ciulli is a real cost, since cereblon is the pillar behind glues and Ciulli's VHL ligands made rational design teachable, and a citation limited to bifunctional degraders will look incomplete to the glue community. For B047, the 2020 CRISPR prize is a close precedent, the Kondo and Nishida cytidine-deamination priority claim is unresolved, and clinical outcomes are young. Finally, Car-Parrinello (B061) and sequencing (B063) are mature and arguably overdue compared with both of my parts.

responses.point: Linke prefers B020 as the whole prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and treats the PROTAC and cereblon glue strands as one principle sharing a ternary-complex mechanism; he lists B047 as an alternative and worries about CRISPR closeness and the Kondo and Nishida claim.
responses.response: The shared ternary-complex mechanism is a fair argument, and it is the best case for a Handa seat; if the committee takes a single-part B020, I would accept Crews, Deshaies and Handa. I still prefer to keep the citation on the heterobifunctional concept, because identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target explains how existing drugs act, whereas the 2001 proposal is a design principle, and I think the second is the achievement a citation can state in one sentence. On B047, the Kondo and Nishida claim concerns cytidine deamination by a different construct, and it does not touch the adenine base editor that required evolving a DNA adenine deaminase, so I do not think it should keep Liu out.

responses.point: Aqvist names Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for B020, argues that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made rational degrader design possible, and calls base editing a strong choice for a later year because Liu is the decisive figure.
responses.response: I agree with Johan that Liu alone is the right attribution, and that point settles my own round-1 hesitation about naming trainees. I take the Ciulli argument seriously and it is the strongest alternative to my two-name B020; the difference between us is that I weigh who conceived the principle above who made it routine in design. On waiting, I do not see why base editing should be deferred: independent replication and patient use are already in hand, and I would not make a mature principle wait because a larger clinical record is coming.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports B020 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and raises the concern that it is medicinal chemistry and pharmacology that a Medicine committee could equally claim.
responses.response: I think the Medicine concern is answered by what the citation says. If it names the mechanism, a small molecule that induces a ligase-target ternary complex and drives catalytic degradation, it describes a chemical principle, with ternary-complex cooperativity and linker design as the chemistry. A citation phrased around drugs or disease would be the Medicine version. I would also remind Peter that I withdrew from nitrogenase only on attribution, not on science, and that I would welcome it in a future year.

responses.point: Somfai proposes Buchwald and Hartwig for C-N cross-coupling as a mature, cleanly attributed two-name prize, and acknowledges the objection that it extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize and that Kosugi preceded them.
responses.response: The attribution is as clean as Peter says, and I agree that the science is mature. My difficulty is the one he raises himself, that a second cross-coupling prize rewards a refinement of a recognised principle, while degradation and base editing each introduce a principle not previously recognised. If the committee decides it wants a mature, cleanly attributed prize, I would rank B061 and B063 before B044, because those two are not second prizes in an already honoured area.

responses.point: Sparr makes B020 the whole prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa and says the bifunctional and glue strands explain two complementary halves of one mechanism.
responses.response: I follow that reading and it explains the convergence on Handa. Where I differ is on whether the two halves are one achievement: the PROTAC strand is designed, the cereblon strand was found after the drugs were in use, and a single citation that spans both runs the risk she names, that it reads as a compromise. That is why I would keep the citation to the design principle and would rather use the third seat for Liu than for a glue strand that the committee may be able to honour on its own later.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a single-part B020 with a third named seat (Handa or Ciulli) over my two-part configuration; I would accept Crews, Deshaies and Handa as a single-part prize.
Whether base editing is judged distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and how the unresolved Kondo and Nishida claim should bear on a Liu-only attribution.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader and the still-young base editing clinical record make either part premature.
My attribution and priority details come from general knowledge and the committee statements, and have not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted laureate on my preferred configuration. My own field, dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase, and my collaborations with Rothstein and Stillman, lie outside the shortlisted work. I have a general professional interest in nucleotide chemistry and LC-MS/MS methods, and no recusal is needed. This is unchanged from round 1.
